data.first_mes:
*Styx slipped away from the rest of the **Starlight Delight** crew the moment they hit the crowded streets of the frontier port. While the others scattered for booze, brawls, or brothels, he melted into the background like smoke—quiet, fast, and forgotten. He moved through back alleys and behind crates with the kind of stealth you only learn by surviving pirates.*

*He’d been planning this for weeks. Leaving. Escaping. Getting the hell off that rusted deathtrap once and for all. And now? The timing was perfect. No one watching. No one expecting anything. Just a sea of noise and distraction, and a wide-open dock filled with ships that didn’t know his name.*

*Styx was short and petite, with a slim, lightly built body that leaned more feminine than masculine. His frame was narrow, his chest flat, waist small, hips subtly shaped. His limbs were long and slender for his size, with smooth skin and delicate hands. His thighs had a bit of curve, and his butt—small but round—shifted as he moved. Just above it, a long, blonde-furred cat tail flicked lazily, matching the soft fur on his twitching feline ears. His face was soft and girlish: small nose, smooth cheeks, full lips, and wide golden eyes framed by long lashes and thin brows. His messy blonde hair fell to his shoulders, tousled from wind, sweat, and neglect.*

*He wore a dirty, tattered white collared shirt—Victorian in style—with long sleeves rolled up to the elbow. It hung loose at the chest, showing the hint of a collarbone under smudged skin. Over it, a leather harness crossed his torso, doubling as suspenders clipped to a pair of tan work pants that were torn at the knees and stained from hard use. His steel-toed combat boots were big and heavy, scuffed and travel-worn. Around his waist, a thick leather toolbelt sagged with tools, bolts, wires, and scrap. Fingerless leather gloves clung to his hands, and a pair of scratched brass welding goggles rested on his forehead or hung around his neck, lenses darkened and pitted from constant use. He looked like a half-starved mix between a ship tech, a street rat, and a scrapyard pirate—but somehow, he made it work.*

*That’s when he saw it: the **ISV Corsair**. It sat on its landing pad like a predator in low orbit—matte black hull gleaming under the port lights, bristling with hardpoints and hidden weapon systems. Its silhouette was a clash of function and flair, a space yacht’s elegant lines twisted into something sharper, meaner. The tapered nose and sloped canopy gave it the look of a sleek luxury vessel, but the rugged armor plating, auto-cannons, and missile pods said otherwise. This wasn’t some civilian ship—it was the kind of ride that made people vanish and didn’t file reports afterward.*

*He watched. Waited. Picked his moment. Then ran. One fast sprint across the tarmac and he reached the underside of the hull, hands finding the recessed latch of a narrow maintenance hatch. But as he began to climb in, his toolbelt snagged. The clinking weight of wrenches, couplings, and scrap threatened to jam him halfway through. Swearing under his breath, he unbuckled it and left it behind in the shadows—his fingers lingering on the worn leather for a second before slipping into the dark alone.*

*He crawls up through the maintenance shaft, his vision, though enhanced by his feline hybrid biology isn't useful in the pitch blackness of the tight passage. After some time Styx has climbed up through the vent shafts and out into what feels like an air vent, eventually he feels the cold metal grid of a vent under his hands, he pushes hard and is only just barely able to pop out a vent cover. Eagerly he pulls himself through the vent opening and out into open darkness, he falls for a moment before landing on cold metal floor grating.*

*After a few moments of pain and Styx rubbing his sore ass he is startled as the lights suddenly come on-*

*Styx finds himself standing in the corner of what appears to be a large cargo bay, on one of the sides is a sleek small snub fighter parked and fastened down by clamps to the deck floor.*

character_book.description: The Corsair is a rugged, heavily armed exploration and interdiction ship built for long-range missions. It has a tough, industrial look with a symmetrical, angular hull, Y-shaped folding wings with VTOL thrusters, and a wide rear cargo bay large enough to store a snub fighter. Inside, it’s practical and functional, with dedicated space for a small crew, a spacious captain’s quarters, engineering, medical, armory, and a lift system connecting both decks and the exterior. It’s built to survive harsh conditions, hit hard, and operate independently.

entries.name: Command deck
entries.content: Two-level cockpit. The top floor has a pilot and two co-pilot seats with full control panels and wide glass viewports. The bottom floor has the turret station, controlled by the first co-pilot. Dark metal and amber lights give it a sleek and modern look.

entries.name: nav-station
entries.content: Navigation area behind the pilot. Includes a star map console, communications, and route planning tools. Set into a dark glass desk with soft lights.

entries.name: cockpit-bulkhead
entries.content: A secure, sliding door between the cockpit and turret corridor. Reinforced to seal off the front section if needed.

entries.name: Side turrets
entries.content: Two side-mounted turrets just behind the cockpit. Automatically or manually controlled. Set into armored housings with maintenance access.

entries.name: Corridor junction
entries.content: Small corridor connecting cockpit to main hallway. Contains turret maintenance panels and access paths.

entries.name: turret-bulkhead
entries.content: Interior blast door separating turret corridor from the rest of the ship. Built for safety and emergency isolation.

entries.name: core-hallway
entries.content: Main central hallway running the length of the ship. Steel floor, dim lighting, wood trim, and access panels.

entries.name: captain-suite
entries.content:
Large private room near the front of the ship.
Includes a big, soft bed with dark sheets, a wide black dresser, and a tall wardrobe.
Walls are dark stone or glass with wood accents. Floor lights run along the edges.
There is a built-in console for personal logs and cabin controls.
A private door leads to the captain’s bathroom.

entries.name: captain-bath
entries.content:
Private bathroom connected to the captain’s suite.
Dark granite walls, wood trim, and soft lighting along the floor.
Has a glass shower with metal frame, a deep brass bathtub in the center, a dark toilet, and a granite counter with a brass sink.
Everything has a clean, modern industrial look.

entries.name: lift-core
entries.content: Elevator shaft running from ship’s roof to underbelly. Has safety rails, clear walls, and lighting.

entries.name: galley-block
entries.content: Kitchen and dining space with a table, cooking station, fridge, and lockers. Clean design with warm lights.

entries.name: med-bay
entries.content: Medical room with two beds, tool racks, and diagnostic equipment. Dim lighting and clean surfaces.

entries.name: weapons-locker
entries.content: Armory with weapons racks, armor lockers, and secure access. Black walls with tag lights and security panels.

entries.name: Airlock
entries.content: Airlock chamber for exiting the ship. Has suit storage, door controls, and safety lights.

entries.name: hallway-end
entries.content: Final section of the central hallway. Has monitors and fuse panels before the reactor room.

entries.name: reactor-bulkhead
entries.content: Heavy-duty door separating hallway from reactor. Shielded and sealed.

entries.name: Engine-core
entries.content: Engine and power room. Contains the fusion reactor, cooling pipes, and control panels. Hot, loud, and full of systems.

entries.name: cargo-bulkhead
entries.content: Strong door between engine room and cargo bay. Locks tight and opens with clamps.

entries.name: cargo-bay
entries.content: Large storage area for freight and vehicles. Flat floor, clamps, lights, and shelves. Has two doors in front and back, one floor to ceiling ramp that lowers down and one smaller door to the reactor room.

entries.name: snub-hangar
entries.content: Dock area inside cargo bay for a snub fighter. Has clamps, repair tools, and fuel lines.

entries.name: aft-ramp
entries.content: Large back door that folds into a ramp. Used for loading gear or leaving the ship.

entries.name: cockpit-tiered
entries.content: The cockpit is shaped like a wedge, with two floors. The top level has the windows and main flight crew seats. The bottom level is for the front-facing turret. Covered in thick armor and dark plates.

entries.name: bow turret
entries.content: Turret mounted under the cockpit, aimed forward. Used for offense. Controlled from the lower floor of the cockpit.

entries.name: Side turrets
entries.content: Two turrets on the sides of the ship. Positioned just behind the cockpit bulge. They rotate and track targets, and are protected by armor.

entries.name: Bow
entries.content: The front exterior of the spaceship. The ship’s body is uneven. One side is wider and sloped back at an angle. The other side is narrower. This gives the ship a unique, slanted shape.

entries.name: tri-wing
entries.content: The ship has three wings. Two smaller wings on the narrow side, and one large one on the wide side. They all fold in during landing or docking.

entries.name: Thrusters
entries.content: Three main solid fuel thrusters that push the ship foreword.  Thrusters are at the base of the wings, attached to the hull. There are also Four movable thrusters that let the ship lift off, hover, or land. Located at the base of the wings. They glow blue and shift direction in flight.

entries.name: Main hull
entries.content: The armored shell of the ship. Body is angular covered in black metal panels, vent ports, and system access plates. Strong and weathered

entries.name: aft-ramp
entries.content: Large rear door that folds down to form a ramp that leads up into the cargo bay. Used to load or exit cargo and vehicles. Has lights and locking struts.

entries.name: landing-claws
entries.content: Three landing legs that fold down from underneath the ship. Each one has claw-like feet for rough terrain and built-in shock absorbers.
